pledges.title: £210m high-streets package
pledges.owner: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
pledges.verbatimQuote: The £210m package confirmed today is from MHCLG funding already earmarked for high street support and regeneration.
pledges.sourceTitle: Boarded-up high streets brought back to life with £210m boost (GOV.UK, 25 Sep 2026)
pledges.notes: Per the release, this is existing MHCLG funding already earmarked for high streets, not additional money. No allocation to named recipients found as of last check.

pledges.title: Derelict Buildings Fund
pledges.owner: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
pledges.verbatimQuote: Through the new £125m Derelict Buildings Fund, government will support local authorities to transform these buildings into what their communities need, from health centres to civic spaces.
pledges.sourceTitle: Boarded-up high streets brought back to life with £210m boost (GOV.UK, 25 Sep 2026)
pledges.notes: No prospectus, bidding round or allocations found as of last check.

pledges.title: Community rescue of at-risk buildings and businesses
pledges.owner: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
pledges.verbatimQuote: An additional £65m will be invested in helping communities right across England rescue and revamp beloved buildings and businesses at risk of closure, like pubs and sports clubs.
pledges.sourceTitle: Boarded-up high streets brought back to life with £210m boost (GOV.UK, 25 Sep 2026)
pledges.notes: The release names pubs and sports clubs as examples; it does not name shops. Delivery route not yet published.

pledges.title: High Street Rental Auctions
pledges.owner: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
pledges.verbatimQuote: And a further £20 million will be split equally between High Street Rental Auctions, letting out properties vacant for 12 months or more, and a new Co-operative Development Programme so local people share in their high street’s success.
pledges.sourceTitle: Boarded-up high streets brought back to life with £210m boost (GOV.UK, 25 Sep 2026)
pledges.notes: The release does not state £10m for this line directly; £10m is derived from '£20 million … split equally' between it and the Co-operative Development Programme.

pledges.title: Regional Co-operative Development Programme
pledges.owner: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
pledges.verbatimQuote: The £10 million regional Co-operative Development Programme will help mayors and strategic authorities set up more co-operative businesses, owned and run by the staff, customers and communities who use them, so local people share directly in their high street’s success.
pledges.sourceTitle: Boarded-up high streets brought back to life with £210m boost (GOV.UK, 25 Sep 2026)
pledges.notes: To be delivered through mayors and strategic authorities. No allocation per authority found as of last check.

pledges.title: Sussex & Brighton long-term investment fund
pledges.owner: UK Government (devolution deal) — Sussex & Brighton Strategic Authority
pledges.verbatimQuote: A long-term investment fund totalling £1.14 billion, providing sustained long-term ‑term funding for locally agreed priorities.
pledges.sourceTitle: Parliamentary milestone reached as Sussex and Brighton move closer to devolution (East Sussex County Council, 12 Feb 2026)

evidence.label: SBSA, 30 Jun 2026: £117m is "just one part of the £1.14 billion secured over the next 30 years"

pledges.notes: Quote reproduced as published, including the duplicated "long-term ‑term". Spread over 30 years. The £30.4m and £117m lines below are reported as parts of this settlement, but how they nest is not stated in one place, so they are recorded as separate pledges.

pledges.title: £30.4m released before the first mayoral election
pledges.owner: UK Government (devolution deal) — Sussex & Brighton Strategic Authority
pledges.verbatimQuote: £30.4 million released over the next two years before mayoral elections, enabling early investment in programmes that matter most to Sussex residents and businesses.
pledges.sourceTitle: Parliamentary milestone reached as Sussex and Brighton move closer to devolution (East Sussex County Council, 12 Feb 2026)
pledges.notes: Not found on sussexandbrighton-cca.gov.uk itself as of last check; the source is a constituent council's release reporting ministers' commitment. Whether it sits inside the £117m four-year budget is not stated.

pledges.title: Capacity funding to establish the authority
pledges.owner: UK Government (devolution deal) — Sussex & Brighton Strategic Authority
pledges.verbatimQuote: £9.0 million in capacity funding over four years to support the establishment and operation of the new authority.
pledges.sourceTitle: Parliamentary milestone reached as Sussex and Brighton move closer to devolution (East Sussex County Council, 12 Feb 2026)
pledges.notes: Amount unconfirmed: other council releases about the same deal give £4.5 million in capacity funding over four years. Recorded as unknown until the authority's budget papers settle it.

pledges.title: First four years of devolution funding
pledges.verbatimQuote: The £117 million represents the first four years of government funding secured for the area through the formation of the Authority.
pledges.sourceTitle: Sussex & Brighton Strategic Authority unlocks access to £117 million for the Sussex area (SBSA, 30 Jun 2026)
pledges.notes: Announced at the authority's first AGM (the release is dated 30 Jun; its text gives the AGM as Wednesday 1 July). The release cites budget documents; those have not yet been checked line by line here.

pledges.title: Bus franchising appraisal funding
pledges.owner: Department for Transport — Sussex & Brighton Strategic Authority
pledges.verbatimQuote: The Bus Franchising Support Funding package includes £500,000 for the studies and £64,000 to recruit a dedicated Bus Reform Officer to lead the work.

evidence.label: SBSA, 9 Oct 2026: "awarded more than half a million pounds from the Government to develop a bus reform plan"

pledges.notes: The authority states it has secured the money from DfT. No published studies or Bus Reform Officer appointment found yet.

pledges.title: Local Transport Delivery Plan
pledges.verbatimQuote: The plan brings together the transport programmes of Brighton & Hove City Council, East Sussex County Council and West Sussex County Council, setting out around £455 million of investment over the next four years.
pledges.sourceTitle: Nearly £100 million for buses across Sussex (SBSA, 9 Oct 2026)
pledges.notes: Approved by the SBSA Board on 8 Oct 2026. The release says the schemes were already developed and agreed by the three councils; the plan consolidates them rather than adding new money.

pledges.title: Bus funding across Sussex
pledges.verbatimQuote: Buses are one of the biggest areas of investment, with nearly £100 million of bus funding planned across the region.
pledges.sourceTitle: Nearly £100 million for buses across Sussex (SBSA, 9 Oct 2026)
pledges.notes: "Nearly" £100m: includes almost £40m over three years for services, £39m for bus priority and stops, and almost £6m for local fare offers.
